issue-4604: Two identical coffees on the same day count as one transaction?

name: code_read_file

input.title: Don't collapse genuinely repeated transactions in dedupe
input.body:
File: src/ingest/dedupe.ts

dedupe() treats any two rows with the same date, amount and description as the same transaction and drops the second one outright. That's correct for an overlapping-statement re-upload, but it also silently discards legitimate repeated purchases (e.g. two identical coffees bought the same morning), losing real transaction data from the report.

Proposed change: instead of a plain Set of keys, count occurrences of each key per dedupe run and only drop a row once it exceeds the number of times that same key already exists in `seen`/`existing` (i.e. treat a repeat beyond what was already imported as new, not a repeat within the same new batch). This preserves multiple identical same-day transactions while still catching true re-imports of the same file.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/dedupe.ts

That's an answer to your question, but it points at a real bug: dedupe() in src/ingest/dedupe.ts builds a key from date + amount + description and drops any row whose key it has already seen. That's meant to catch the same statement being uploaded twice, but it has the side effect you hit — two genuinely separate purchases that happen to share date, amount and description (your two coffees) collapse into one, and the second is silently dropped rather than kept. Opened a PR proposing to count occurrences instead of using a plain seen-set, so only imports beyond what was already stored are treated as duplicates.

text:
Triaged issue #4604:

- **Label:** bug
- **File:** `src/ingest/dedupe.ts` — the dedupe key is just `date|amount|description`, so legitimately repeated same-day transactions (like two identical coffee purchases) are indistinguishable from an accidental re-import and get dropped.
- **PR:** pr-9 (`repomind/issue-4604`) proposing to count occurrences per key instead of using a plain seen-set, so only imports beyond the already-stored count are treated as true duplicates.
- **Comment:** posted explaining the root cause and linking the fix.
